subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static pickup truck model with hover thrusters instead of wheels, roughly 5.4m long, 2m wide, 1.9m tall, making sure the lowest points sit exactly at floor level.

I'm now blocking out the body: a dark chassis box, then an extruded side-profile silhouette for the hood, cab, and bed sections with specific z-ranges and heights to create the pickup shape.

Still working out body and cab geometry...

I'll nudge the glass front edge slightly forward to avoid z-fighting with the slope, giving it a cyan emissive tint. Then I'm planning the roof rack with a cyan light bar, bed side walls, tailgate, headboard, and armor details like a roll bar and sweeping-barrel turret gun, finished with olive/desert camo paneling for the military look.

For paint I'm layering mottled olive-dark-tan patches for camo, plus a cyberpunk variant with neon magenta/cyan stripe boxes and a "UNIT 07" decal, alongside a hood scoop, bull bar, and glowing head/taillights. For propulsion I'm replacing wheels with four corner-mounted ducted-fan hover nacelles—lathed ring housings with glowing cyan fan discs underneath, cross-box blades, and struts connecting each pod to the chassis.

Now I'm checking the geometry so the wider nacelle rings don't clash with the narrower body, adding fender pylons and rear thrust nozzles, and placing a thin magenta underglow box beneath the chassis for the lighting effect.

I'm positioning front and rear nacelles, then adding small details like an antenna, side mirrors, thin dark door seam boxes, a handle, and a decal plane for the door emblem.

Placing the emblem plane just off the cab's side face, and deciding to skip text in favor of simple symmetric shapes like chevrons or a star to avoid mirroring issues on the opposite door.

I'm also planning a hood decal with warning-chevron stripes positioned on the flat top section, plus a rear plate detail, keeping a helper function for boxes and part count manageable around 120, and making sure glow effects work on flat-colored parts.

Now I'm capping the palette to 64 flat colors and writing helper functions for boxes and extrusions, then setting up a mirrored gun turret with twin barrels extending forward from the bed using rod geometry.

Checking barrel placement against the cab roof, I realize a forward-pointing barrel would be too short before hitting the cab, so I'm reconsidering the design as an angled missile pod instead — a tilted launcher box with six glowing tube tips, working out the rotation angle needed to point it upward and forward.

Computing the direction vector for a 40° tilt and orienting the launcher box and its tube array along that angled axis, arranging a 3x2 grid of cylinders as the tube openings...

Now I'm adding the front details: a bull bar frame with horizontal and upright bars, glowing headlights in white-cyan, a dark grille, red taillights at the rear, and a thin neon strip running along the side.

I'm positioning door armor plates on the body sides in olive, checking placement against the cab width and window area to avoid overlaps.

Now I'm importing metal and panelled materials from the clockwork kit for the chassis and armor pieces, then setting up the camo pattern with olive, dark green, and tan patches with a small gap to blend edges. For the final touches, I'm adding rear exhaust cylinders with glowing discs aligned along the z-axis, an antenna rod, and a roof light bar with magenta and cyan glowing segments before exporting the完整 build.
